motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Easing for the connector wipe and the pill reveal.

motion.name: stage-run
motion.value: stage-run 0.9s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) backwards (clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0) to inset(0))

motion.name: job-pass
motion.value: job-pass 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) backwards (opacity 0.35, saturate(0), translateY(4px) to rest)
motion.purpose: A stage's pills rise from grey to full colour when the stage settles.

motion.name: node-step
motion.purpose: Time each stage node shows its spinner before revealing its final status; stages are staggered by the same step.

motion.name: spin-slow
motion.purpose: The spinner on the current stage and its status line.

motion.name: action-lift
motion.value: transform: translateY(-1px) on hover, 0 on active
motion.purpose: Hover response of orange action controls.

motion.name: disclosure-chevron
motion.purpose: Chevron on a job panel header.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every node shows its final status immediately.

narrative.overview:
The site borrows the run view of a CI/CD tool and uses it to tell a career. Employers are stages in time order, each shipped thing is a job with a status icon and a log you can open, and the final stage is a manual job the visitor triggers. The borrowed form is doing real work: status is the one visual vocabulary, so a hiring lead reads "done", "current" and "in progress" from icon and stroke before reading a word.

Two fields carry the page. A saturated deploy green opens and closes it, edge to edge, holding the sticky top bar, the name, the pipeline graph and the contact close. Between them the body is a pale green-grey sheet with white panels and near-black green ink. Colour is rationed: green is the place, amber means unfinished, orange means "your move", and nothing else is tinted. The surfaces are flat, corners are small, and there are no shadows, gradients or decorative images.

The backoffice lives in the same world at lower volume. It drops the green field entirely, keeps the pale sheet, white panels, the same three typefaces and the same amber "in progress" mark, and spends green only on the current nav item, the save button and switches. Orange never appears there.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed green field at the top and the bottom; pale sheet in between.
Status icons (check, spinner, dashed ring, play) are the system's only iconographic language on the public page.
Solid stroke means finished; dashed stroke means not finished yet.
One orange, reserved for the action the visitor is asked to take.
Hierarchy by scale: a 6rem name against 0.75rem mono metadata, with little in between.
Flat surfaces separated by 1px lines and tonal steps, never by shadow.

rules.name: The Manual Job Rule
rules.body: Orange marks the action the visitor is being asked to take, and only that. It is never a status, a highlight or a decoration, and it does not appear in the backoffice.

rules.name: The Unfinished Is Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber always travels with a dashed stroke and means "not finished yet": a job in progress, a skill still being studied, a certification being prepared, testimonials waiting for review. The one exception in the build is the text-selection highlight.

rules.name: The Field Is A Place Rule
rules.body: Deploy Green is a full-width ground, not a tint. On the public page it appears as an edge-to-edge band or not at all; small green elements on the light sheet use Passed Green.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono is for text the pipeline would print: identifiers, job names, dates, counts, status and log lines. Sentences a person wrote are set in Geist, headings in Bricolage Grotesque.

rules.name: The Scale Not Weight Rule
rules.body: Display faces stay at 600 (500 for the role line). Emphasis comes from the jump in size between levels, not from heavier weights, capitals or letterspacing; nothing in the build is uppercased or tracked out.

rules.name: The Flat Run Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are separated by tone and by 1px lines. If a new element seems to need a shadow to read, change its fill by one tonal step instead.

rules.name: The Final State First Rule
rules.body: Animation only ever delays or reveals content that is already in the markup in its finished state. Nothing depends on an animation finishing to become visible or correct.

rules.name: The Solid Or Dashed Rule
rules.body: A dashed outline is a claim that something is unfinished or absent. Never dash a border for texture, and never draw an unfinished thing with a solid amber fill.

dos: Do open and close a public page with the full-bleed Deploy Green field (#0b6b3a) and keep everything between on the pale sheet (#eef2ee) with white panels.
Do express state with the four status icons and with stroke style: solid for finished, dashed for unfinished.
Do pair amber borders with Amber Ink (#6f4a00) for any text on light surfaces; amber itself is a border and icon colour only.
Do keep orange (#ff4d1f) for controls that ask the visitor to act, with dark ink (#10201a) on top and a play icon in front.
Do set identifiers, dates, counts and log lines in Geist Mono at 0.75rem to 0.9375rem, and everything a person wrote in Geist.
Do separate surfaces with 1px rules and one-step tonal changes; keep corners at 0.45rem, 0.325rem when nested.
Do use the shared 72rem container and the label-column plus content-column split (17rem or 12rem beside a fluid column, 3rem gap) for new sections.
Do make every animated element correct in its final state without the animation, and honour reduced motion.
Do keep the backoffice on the pale sheet with white panels, green for the current item and for saving, and written labels beside every state.
donts: Don't use orange for status, emphasis, links or anything in the backoffice.
Don't use a dashed outline as decoration, or show an unfinished item with a solid outline.
Don't put Deploy Green behind a card, a badge or a partial-width block on the public page; it is a full-width field.
Don't add shadows, gradients, blur or glass to layout surfaces.
Don't set sentences or headings in Geist Mono, and don't uppercase or letterspace labels.
Don't add heavier display weights; go up a size instead.
Don't introduce a fifth status, a second accent colour or coloured tags for technologies; skills are neutral chips.
Don't rely on colour alone for state: every status has an icon and a text label.
